summary: The note describes the Duchy of Magdeburg, a territory that was a province of the Margraviate of Brandenburg from 1680 to 1701 and a province of the Kingdom of Prussia from 1701 to 1807. It arose when the Archbishopric of Magdeburg was secularized by Brandenburg, and its capitals were Magdeburg and Halle. The duchy was dissolved during the Napoleonic Wars in 1807, and its territory became part of the Province of Saxony in 1815.
one_line: Historical duchy formed from the secularized Archbishopric of Magdeburg, governed under Brandenburg and Prussia until 1807.
key_facts: The Duchy of Magdeburg was a province of the Margraviate of Brandenburg from 1680 to 1701.
The Duchy of Magdeburg was a province of the German Kingdom of Prussia from 1701 to 1807.
The Duchy of Magdeburg replaced the Archbishopric of Magdeburg after its secularization by Brandenburg.
The capitals of the Duchy of Magdeburg were Magdeburg and Halle.
Burg was described as another important town of the Duchy of Magdeburg.
The Duchy of Magdeburg was dissolved during the Napoleonic Wars in 1807.
The territory of the Duchy of Magdeburg was made part of the Province of Saxony in 1815.
